主要内容: Wal-Mart has agreed to contribute $25 million to settle lawsuits related to gas can explosions. The settlement is part of a $161 million fund aimed at resolving claims against Blitz USA, the former largest manufacturer of plastic gas cans. The company, now bankrupt, faced numerous lawsuits over alleged product defects. Wal-Mart, the largest seller of these cans, did not admit any safety issues with the product. The settlement includes contributions from various parties, including Blitz USA's estate and insurers, while denying liability for the injuries. Wal-Mart officials stated that the responsibility for product safety rested with the manufacturers. Legal experts argue that the inclusion of flame arresters could have prevented many of the incidents. Wal-Mart's spokesperson acknowledged awareness of the incidents since 2005 but stated the company did not request safety improvements from manufacturers. The settlement covers individuals injured by gas can explosions between July 2007 and July 2012. The Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) reported at least 11 deaths and 1,200 emergency room visits linked to gas can explosions during gasoline pouring since 1998. Wal-Mart officials stated that the company did not ask Blitz to add flame arresters to reduce the risk of flashback explosions. However, in a 2003 internal video, a Wal-Mart employee humorously referenced a gas can explosion. The CPSC initially did not act on the issue in 2011 but later recommended adding flame arresters to portable gas cans following an NBC News investigation.
